name: python-code-type
body: Add a `py` arm to the ingestor's built-in code-type classifier (builtin_code_type, src/classify.rs) so accepted Python sources are in the graph and filterable rather than dropped: test = a *_test.py / test_* / *.test.py filename or a test|tests|__tests__ path segment; generated = a __pycache__|gen|generated path segment; external = a vendor|third_party|thirdparty path segment; else src. A `.pyi` stub filename is NOT itself a generated marker: hand-written / typeshed API stubs are first-class source that `ty` consumes like any module (python-accept-extensions) and every class/def in a stub carries full location fields (python-frontend-evidence), so a `.pyi` classifies `src` — the exact analog of the TS arm leaving `.d.ts` as `src`. `generated` stays scoped to genuine tool output by path segment: a `.pyi` under a __pycache__|gen|generated tree still classifies generated. `site-packages` is deliberately NOT in this arm: it is a discovery exclusion and is never a scan root (domain.constraint.python-exclusions), so no site-packages path ever reaches the classifier and the segment would be dead prose. The existing config-replaces-built-ins behaviour is unchanged (an apg/config.json replaces the built-ins entirely). All-code-included holds within the discovered tree: every Python file not under a discovery exclusion is scanned and filtered by code_type, never dropped for provenance. AC: an ordinary src module classifies src; a *_test.py classifies test; a hand-written .pyi stub classifies src (never generated), as does a .pyi consumed as a module; a .pyi under a gen/ or generated/ tree classifies generated; a file under third_party/ classifies external; a file under site-packages produces no node (excluded from discovery, not classified external); none of the accepted files is absent from the graph.
